[1/6] Plan: living Syndicate contracts - specific targets/objectives, risk tiers, deadlines, rush bonus, expiry consequences, trust-scaled payouts, CLI/Web clocks, tests, ADR-020

impact_assessment.why: Mechanics audit: the Syndicate contract is the only persistent goal besides static story quests, but after the initial job it degrades to a generic random node-type with no specific target, no deadline, no rush decision, and no relationship stake. That makes the largest reward source repetitive and removes time pressure from the clock/lay_low layer; operative trust is almost cosmetic. Deadlines also give the market, shifts, and downtime real opportunity cost.
impact_assessment.benefits: Adds a replayable risk/reward job loop with explicit targets, rotating objectives, deadline tension, rush bonuses, and trust that changes payout and deadline terms; makes lay_low and loud play trade against a job clock; gives landed contracts narrative attribution through their giver.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: BountyContract and GameState/state payload gain additive fields (old saves default to no deadline); generated contracts gain specific target_ip/target_file/objective, so legacy completion paths need an objective fallback; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: server state mutations stay under the existing session lock; state: contract reward now depends on giver trust and completion turn, so tests that pin exact payouts must pin trust/rush conditions
impact_assessment.mitigation: Explicit backward-compatible objective inference, a dedicated world_rng contract stream to protect reward determinism, centralized contract finalization, failing-first unit/CLI/API tests, full discover after each milestone, and ADR-020.

[1/5] Plan: Syndicate job board - three rotating offers, accept/decline choice, offer shelf life, deadline start on acceptance, CLI/Web/API surfaces, tests, ADR-021

impact_assessment.why: The contract market still auto-assigns a single job, so risk tiers and givers are not a player choice. An offer board adds autonomy, makes risk/reward selection legible, and gives declining a real broker-relationship cost.
impact_assessment.benefits: Players choose risk tier, objective, target, and giver; offers rotate on the clock; active jobs still have a hard deadline; trust remains the payout/deadline currency.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: GameState.contract_offers additive; BountyContract gains offer/accept fields; completing or expiring a job now leaves active_contract None until acceptance; existing tests that assume auto-dispatch need updating; dependency: none; concurrency: server mutations stay under the session lock; state: offers persist and must default for old saves
impact_assessment.mitigation: Backward-compatible defaults, a single offer generator reused by initial/refresh paths, explicit lifecycle tests, CLI/API tests, full discover after each milestone, and ADR-021.

[1/5] Plan: close offer-board gaps - paid single-offer drop, persisted contract sequence for unique IDs, trust tiers with dialogue/second favor, and a recon fallback objective for exhausted grids; tests, CLI/Web, ADR-022

impact_assessment.why: Residual gaps: players cannot pass a single bad offer, IDs can collide after reload, trust has no dialogue/unlock effect, and a fully stripped grid stops posting work.
impact_assessment.benefits: A complete choice loop, collision-free IDs, relationship progression with a real unlock, and a repeatable low-risk contract when the grid has no fresh breach/extract/wipe target.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: GameState.contract_seq/ContactProfile bonus favor/Quest? additive, BountyContract objective recon reuses existing objective field; offer drop spends banked Creds; dependency: none; concurrency: server actions stay under the session lock; state: new additive fields default for old saves, recon completion captures the active contract before its tick
impact_assessment.mitigation: Backward-compatible defaults, dedicated offer-drop and recon tests, storage round-trip for contract_seq, full discover after each milestone, and ADR-022.
